dress_code.women: Sarees or salwar kameez with dupatta.
dress_code.men: Dhotis, panchas, or formal shirts and trousers. Lungis, shorts, and sleeveless tops are strictly prohibited.

dos: Do trekking in groups and complete Upper Ahobilam visits well before sunset due to wild animals.
Do hire a local guide for the strenuous trek to Jwala Narasimha and Ugra Sthambham.
Do wear sturdy, slip-resistant walking shoes or sandals for trekking (footwear is removed outside individual shrines).
Do carry sufficient drinking water to prevent dehydration during the mountain climbs.
Do protect your belongings and prasadams from wild monkeys in the forest paths.
donts: Don't litter the forest or Nallamala hill reserve paths with plastics, bottles, or food packets.
Don't attempt to climb Ugra Sthambham if you suffer from vertigo, high blood pressure, or breathing issues.
Don't venture off the marked trekking pathways into the deep forest areas.
Don't take photographs inside the inner cave sanctums of the Narasimha shrines.
Don't stay overnight in the Upper Ahobilam forest area; all visitors must return to Lower Ahobilam before dark.
forest_restrictions: Ahobilam is in a tiger reserve forest zone. Devotees are not allowed to stay or trek in Upper Ahobilam after sunset.
